clue.text: Cutting instrument found in the hold

definitions.meaning: a pair of blades pivoted together for cutting paper or cloth
a wrestling grip in which the legs are locked round an opponent

explanation.surface: A blade turns up in a ship's cargo space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' tempts you below decks on a ship; it is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The common cutting tool shares its name with a wrestler's leg grip, the scissors hold.

clue.text: Listen to Mark on old dulcimer

indicators.note: the solver must hear a word for mark spoken, then write the same-sounding instrument

parts.note: a symbol is a mark or sign

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear a mark made on an antique stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cymbalo is a hammered stringed instrument, a type of dulcimer.

clue.text: Plaster with paste in knockabout comedy

parts.note: to plaster something is to slap it on
to paste is to stick

explanation.surface: Daubing paste on someone as part of a slapstick routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, full of pratfalls and custard pies.

clue.text: Hood, possibly, for an unfashionable canon

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a canon is a rule or law

explanation.surface: A hood worn by an out-of-date cleric, a canon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is Robin Hood, the legendary English outlaw, and 'canon' is a law, not a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the classic example of a bandit living beyond the law.

clue.text: Seasonal gifts for inferior members?

parts.note: small Christmas presents, but read literally the lower limbs (legs) are what fill hosiery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferior' means lower: the legs are the members that fill hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Christmas presents are put in a hung-up sock, and legs fill hosiery.

clue.text: Abominable swindle backed by promissory notes

indicators.note: backed means the word for swindle is turned to run the other way

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A fraud supported by worthless IOUs is a dreadful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abominable is hateful or repugnant.

clue.text: Joined circle extremely well-known for absorbing poetry

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
verse is poetry

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the extreme letters of well-known

explanation.surface: A famous poetry circle has come together.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'well-known' are W and N, and they take in VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversewn means stitched together with overcast stitches, so seamed.

clue.text: The sort of wine hundreds have left sorrowfully

indicators.note: have left means those hundreds depart from the musical term

parts.note: doloroso is the Italian musical direction meaning sorrowfully
D is the Roman numeral 500, five hundreds

explanation.surface: A wistful note about a wine many have abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLOROSO is a musical direction; D in Roman numerals is 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of sherry.

clue.text: Course director foolishly resents mother being involved

indicators.note: being involved means mother is wrapped up inside the jumbled letters
foolishly means the letters of resents are rearranged without sense

parts.note: Ma is mother

explanation.surface: A golf-course director resents his mother meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests golf or a race; it is a ship's heading, so the definition is a helmsman. 'foolishly' gives STEERSN, which 'being involved' wraps round MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A steersman directs a vessel's course, as a helmsman.

clue.text: Result of reverse in road full of traffic, say

indicators.note: reverse means the road's letters are turned round

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, read as MI

indicators.note: say means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a road full of traffic is packed

explanation.surface: A traffic jam brought on by a car reversing on a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway, written MI; PACKED spoken sounds like PACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is an effect or consequence.

clue.text: Judge abandons jest about major party? All right

indicators.note: about means the trimmed jest goes round the following pieces
abandons means the judge's letter is dropped from the jest

parts.note: a joke is a jest
major is a musical key
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A judge stops joking about a big political party and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major party' is not politics: a major is a key in music, and a do is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-doke is a jokey way of saying OK, agreed.

clue.text: Rick — always a good person in a country ride

indicators.note: in means the pieces sit within the ride

parts.note: a hack is a ride on horseback in the countryside
ay is an old word for always
St, a saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: Rick, a decent sort, always enjoys a ride in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a man's name; it is a stack of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay or straw.

clue.text: A verse in bad odour

indicators.note: in means the pieces are put inside the word for bad

parts.note: milk gone bad is sour

explanation.surface: A poem that has fallen into disrepute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bad odour' reads as one idiom, but 'odour' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A savour is a characteristic smell or taste.

clue.text: Part of 22 — nice example of this order

indicators.note: part of means the letters are lying inside the run of words

parts.note: 22 stands for the answer to 22 Across, STUDIO, followed by the word nice

explanation.surface: Part of a studio's work is a fine example of an architectural order.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answer to 22 Across, STUDIO, followed by NICE, and the letters run across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, with scrolled capitals.

clue.text: Unfairness of being surrounded by only frozen water

parts.note: to be surrounded by something is to be in it
just means only
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Being hemmed in by ice is a cruel unfairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice is a lack of fairness.

clue.text: Row after novelist is found in a blizzard

indicators.note: after places the word for row behind the novelist's name

parts.note: C. P. Snow was a British novelist
a storm is a row or uproar

explanation.surface: An argument with an author out in a blizzard.
explanation.walkthrough: C. P. Snow was an English novelist; 'Row' is a commotion, not an oar stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snow-laden storm.

clue.text: He pesters people in a mountain pass

annotationWithheld.why: He pesters people in a mountain pass (9): MEN (people) in TOR..., but no word gives the second TOR; 'pass' gives nothing found
annotationWithheld.clue: He pesters people in a mountain pass

clue.text: Association member in suit on excursion

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering away, so the letters go off course

explanation.surface: A trade-union member dressed in a suit for a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A unionist is a member of a trade union.

clue.text: Weapon produced by sailor in a dive

parts.note: jack is a name for a sailor, as in Jack Tar
a knife is a weapon

explanation.surface: A sailor in a seedy bar pulls a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' looks like a seedy bar; it is a dive in which the body folds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackknife is a dive in which the body bends double then straightens.

clue.text: Lines obstructed after seizure of power

indicators.note: after places the word for obstructed behind the seizure

parts.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power
let means obstructed, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Railway lines are blocked after a military coup.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming verse lines.

clue.text: Victory emblem worth 25p once

definitions.meaning: a wreath of laurel worn on the head by the winner
the British five-shilling coin, worth 25p after decimalisation

explanation.definitionFit: A victor's wreath is a garland for the head, and the old British coin was worth five shillings.

clue.text: A piece of furniture or something

definitions.meaning: a stand with open shelves for small ornaments

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ornament stand with shelves and an unspecified item.

clue.text: Note in the ABC of Dalton's theory

indicators.note: in means the note is put inside the alphabet range

parts.note: ABC read as the letters A to C
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note on the basics of John Dalton's scientific theory.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dalton proposed the atomic theory of matter; 'ABC' is read as A TO C.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalton's scientific theory held that matter is made of indivisible particles.

clue.text: Where one may paint horses, initially in oils

parts.note: a stud is a collection of horses kept for breeding

indicators.note: initially means take the first letters of in and oils

explanation.surface: An artist painting horses in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's studio is the workroom where pictures are painted.

clue.text: Her aunt left to become a church member

indicators.note: to become means her aunt changes into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An aunt leaves to join a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching.

clue.text: Irradiate uranium used in evil weapon

indicators.note: used in means the uranium is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: ill means evil
a mine is an explosive weapon
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Uranium is used to make a nuclear weapon that irradiates.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is to light up, to shine light upon.

clue.text: Rebellion of posh element in boat

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the boat

parts.note: MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht
U means upper-class
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A posh member of the crew causes a rebellion on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: U is upper-class in British usage; MY stands for motor yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is a rebellion, especially by a ship's crew.

clue.text: Amount of wine presented by former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: How much wine an ex-partner brought round.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means size, scope or degree.

clue.text: Protection for an old place in London, perhaps?

indicators.note: in means the old place sits inside the description of London

parts.note: London is a city in the south-east (SE)
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Guarding an old site in London.
explanation.walkthrough: London is read as SE CITY, a city in the south-east; Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Security means safety or protection from harm.
